the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock.text: Ahoy, young [lad/lass]. Might ye be able to help me, perhaps? I be in a spot of bother.

options.text: Who are you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: I be the Corsair Captain! Captain of the Corsairs of Corsair Cove! My gallant band of corsairs are famed in song and story among all seafarers.

options.text: I've never heard of you.

steps.player: I've never heard of you.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr... well, ye can boast of yer ignorance if ye likes, but it don't make ye sound smarter.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Well, as I were saying, young [lad/lass], I be in a spot of bother, and I thought ye might be able to help.

options.text: That's very interesting; do tell me more.

steps.player: That's very interesting; do tell me more.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Well, as I were saying, young [lad/lass], I be in a spot of bother, and I thought ye might be able to help.

options.text: What kind of help do you need?

steps.player: What kind of help do you need?

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: It be about my crew. They be a lazy bunch at times, but they be stout in the heart and strong in the arm, and they don't deserve what's happened to them...

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: It be a curse! A curse has been laid upon my crew! That's the only thing it can be.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: So I need a young [lad/lass] such as yerself to find a way to lift the curse. Will ye help me?

options.text: Sure, I'll try to help with your curse.

steps.player: Sure, I'll try to help with your curse.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr! Thanks, young [lad/lass]. And a worthy [lad/lass] ye must surely be, brave in the heart and stiff in the spine.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Now, I've a ship moored west of Rimmington. Come and meet me on board, and we'll set off to Corsair Cove.

steps.player: West of Rimmington, you say? Okay, I'll meet you on board your ship there.

steps.text: Captain Tock swaggers off towards Rimmington.

options.text: No, I'm not available.
No, I'm not available.

steps.player: No, I'm not available.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr. Some other time, perhaps...

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: Arrr, ye've found my ship - good [lad/lass]. I used to command a much larger vessel, sailing the seas with my crew of Corsairs, but now we be settled in Corsair Cove.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: My Corsairs be a good crew, but this curse has laid them low, all except me. Sickly, they be. Too weak to stand. Ye'll see fer yerself soon enough.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: There be four of 'em afflicted by the curse - Gnocci, Ithoi, Arsen and young Colin. All taken to their beds, a- mewlin' and a-pukin' like so many babbies.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: I've another crewman, Francois, but he be away on a mission. I hope he be spared!

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: Now be ye ready to voyage to Corsair Cove to help 'em? I can sail ye back here any time ye likes.

options.text: Okay, I'm ready go to Corsair Cove.

steps.player: Okay, I'm ready go to Corsair Cove.

steps.text: The ship sails to Corsair Cove...

options.text: Not just now, thanks.

steps.player: Not just now, thanks.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: That's fair enough, young [lad/lass], but perhaps ye'll return to help me soon...

options.text: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.player: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: I think so. That navigator, Ithoi, always warned us that this kind of thing could happen, but I didn't think it could possibly be real. But now this has happened, and I think it's my fault.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: You should maybe see what Ithoi thinks. He's been cursed too, so I guess he'll be in his hut, off to the south-west, near the shore.

options.text: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.player: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: A sympathetic soul you are. I'm in real pain here.

steps.player: Yes, I hear you've been cursed.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-colin-before-.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-colin-before-.text: I'm sorry! Tell her I'm sorry! Then maybe she'll make the pain stop...

options.text: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.player: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Yes, that's what it must be. Ithoi, the navigator, always told us to beware of curses. You should talk to him - he really knows about these things.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Ithoi lives in the hut to the south-west, nearest to the sea.

options.text: Perhaps you can tell me about it another time.
I hear you've been cursed.

steps.player: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Yes, I think She did this to us. I should have left Her alone. Ithoi told us to beware of this kind of thing.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Ithoi's been cursed too. You can probably find him in his hut, south-west from here.

options.text: My lower intestine!

steps.player: My lower intestine!

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: ... look, I'm in a lot of pain here. We're not playing Name Your Favourite Body Part.

steps.player: Yes, I hear you've been cursed.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-ithoi.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-ithoi.text: Arrr, we be cursed, we be CURSED! It be a curse upon us!

options.text: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.player: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Aye? D'ye think so? Really? Am I not a picture of health an' beauty?

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: YES - WE'VE BEEN CURSED!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: I've sailed the seas all my life. I sailed the seas as a man, like I sailed 'em as a boy.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: I even sailed the seas during that tricky phase in between, when ye'r not quite a man yet, but ye'r not really a boy anymore. But I don't want to talk about that bit.

steps.player: Um...

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: The point I'm makin' is that I know the seas like I know the palm of my hand. I've been to strange lands an' seen things that'll make yer juices turn in yer veins.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: I've seen dancing fish-women, monkey-kings, huge men in turbans from the far West selling treasure maps - you name it, an' I've seen it.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: There be more things in the world than ye dreams of in yer fancy book-learnin'! An' most of 'em be hostile. Could be any number of things brought this curse upon us. Demons, evil spirits, anything!

steps.player: Okay, it doesn't sound like you know what's behind the curse. Thanks.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Arrr!

options.text: I think I'll leave you to get on with it.

steps.player: I think I'll leave you to get on with it.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: ... arrr.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock
the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.text: Have ye any idea about how to lift the curse?

options.text: I've spoken to some of your crew.

the-cursed-crew-talking-to-captain-tock-.speaker: Captain Tock

steps.player: I've met him. He definitely thinks it's a curse, but wasn't able to say exactly what caused it.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: I'm afraid it may be all my fault.

steps.player: Oh?

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Captain Tock had me exploring some caves, west of the cove. I'm a thief, see, like my brother Francois, and the Captain thought I could sneak past the monsters without being noticed.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Well, I climbed down the vines, and found a big cave filled with terrifying ogres!

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: I'd hoped I could use my amazing Thieving skills to avoid them seeing me, but I was out of luck. By the time I'd finished clambering down the ladder, they'd spotted me.

steps.player: So you were trying to explore that ogre cave, and the ogres saw you?

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Yes. I quickly grabbed some loot, so I wouldn't have to face the Captain empty-handed, and fled up the ladder before the ogres could kill me!

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: But a couple of days later we all fell ill. I think what I stole must have been some kind of sacred relic, and the shamans in the cave have cursed us for stealing it.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Maybe you could get the relic back from the Captain, and return it to the ogres? And tell them I'm very sorry. Then perhaps they'll lift the curse.

steps.player: I see.

options.text: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.player: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief

steps.player: Yes, I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Oh dear.

arsen-s-curse-talking-to-arsen-talking-t.text: If the player has not talked to Chief Tess:

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief

arsen-s-curse-talking-to-captain-tock.speaker: Captain Tock
arsen-s-curse-talking-to-captain-tock.text: Have ye any idea about how to lift the curse?

options.text: Arsen says he gave you a sacred ogre relic.

steps.player: Arsen says he gave you a sacred ogre relic.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, that he did. I'd sent him to explore the caves west of the cove, an' he brings me back a bone lump, saying he stole it from the ogre chief.

steps.player: He thinks the ogres have cursed you all because he stole one of their sacred relics, and he wants me to take it back to them now.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, I've no use fer the silly thing. If it'll get the curse lifted, ye can take it right to that ogre chief an' give it back.
Captain Tock gives you the loot that Arsen stole from the ogre chief.

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.
I'll talk to you later.
A man called Arsen told me he'd visited your cave.

steps.player: A man called Arsen told me he'd visited your cave.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Yah, skinny man climb down vine the other day. Little man, big idiot! Hahahaha...

steps.player: He says he's very sorry...

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: He very silly!

steps.player: Perhaps I should come back another time.

options.text: What is this place?
I'll leave you alone, sorry.
I've come to return what Arsen stole.

steps.player: I've come to return what Arsen stole.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Arsen says he's very sorry for stealing from you. Here it is...
You present Tess with Arsen's loot.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Yah, dat little man is big idiot. Climbed down vine, grabbed tooth-pick off Tess and ran away like scared kebbit.

steps.player: You're saying this is a tooth-pick? Not a sacred relic of the ogres? Did your shamans curse the Corsairs for stealing it?

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Dis is tooth-pick. Tess got plenty more. If skinny idiot man want Tess' old tooth-pick, maybe he sick in his head. But Tess not having shamans curse anyone.

steps.player: Oh. Well, I guess Arsen will be pleased to hear he didn't bring the curse upon the Corsairs.

options.text: What is this place?

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Have you returned the sacred relic to the ogres? Will they forgive me and lift the curse?

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.player: Their chief, Tess, says that wasn't a sacred relic at all. It was her tooth-pick.

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Are you telling me the ogres cursed us all because I stole their chief's tooth-pick?

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.player: She didn't care - she's got lots of tooth-picks, and she just thought you were some kind of weirdo when you stole one. They never cursed you at all.

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Oh. That's a relief, I guess. Um... thank you for your help. But I do wonder where the curse really came from.

colin-s-curse-talking-to-colin.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin

options.text: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.player: I've met him. He definitely thinks it's a curse, but wasn't able to say exactly what caused it.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: This is all my fault. But I didn't mean to upset her. I just thought we could be friends. Now I must have upset her, and she's cursed us all!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Ithoi always told us that bad things happen to sailors who get involved with mermaids, but I didn't believe him. I should have listened! But I'll tell you what happened...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin

A flashback to a few nights ago...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Such a beautiful night!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: What lands lie beyond the dim horizon, I wonder...
Colin uses the telescope at Ithoi's hut.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Eh?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: What was that? I'd better have another look.
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Is that what I think it is?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: It's so dark out there, but I think... ... yes, I'm quite sure...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: ... yes, it's a mermaid! She's beautiful!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Hello?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Can you hear me?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: You're the most lovely person I've ever seen!
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I can see you moving your arms, but it's very dark. Are you waving to me?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: kiss*

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Hello?
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Oh, no, I think she's gone away. Did I put her off?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Maybe she doesn't like strangers shouting about her appearance and blowing kisses at her. That might have been rude of me.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I hope she's not angry. Ithoi says mermaids can be dangerous.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin

options.text: Perhaps you can tell me about it another time.

steps.text: Oh. Oh, I see. Okay... I guess that means I didn't upset a mermaid after all. So the curse isn't my fault! Thank you!

steps.player: How are you feeling?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I still feel awful. But I'm glad you've proven it wasn't my fault that we got cursed. I hope you can work out what brought it on us.

steps.player: I'll be on the case.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: C'mon little lobsters. We don't want to keep the Captain waiting! He'll get angry with me again.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.text: Arrr! Ogre women be powerful, an' Arsen be a fool.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.player: I'll carry on trying to solve the curse.
